walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed Penicillium mould killing bacteria.

He couldn't make enough to test on people. In 1941 Florey and Chain mass-produced it. US factories scaled up by D-Day 1944, saving thousands of Allied lives.

The 1942 Beveridge Report attacked five giants including disease.

Labour's Aneurin Bevan launched the NHS on 5 July 1948 — free at the point of use, paid for by tax. It was the world's first fully nationalised health service.

In 1953 Watson and Crick described the DNA double helix.

Keyhole surgery, MRI scanners and the Human Genome Project (2003) followed. Lifestyle diseases — cancer, heart disease, diabetes — became the new battlefront. Anti-smoking laws came in 2007.

Why was Vesalius significant in the history of medicine?
options: His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.
Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.

mcqs.q: What was Pasteur's contribution to medicine?
options: The NHS was originally only for soldiers returning from WWII.
He proved germ theory of disease via experiments on fermentation and spontaneous generation, then developed vaccines for rabies and anthrax — Koch identified specific bacteria.

mcqs.q: Why was the founding of the NHS controversial in 1948?
options: The British Medical Association opposed nationalisation of doctors; Bevan made concessions allowing private practice; Conservatives feared cost and central control.
The NHS was originally only for soldiers returning from WWII.
The NHS was supported by all parties and all doctors from the start.
